Found 5 relevant documentation sections for Vaadin 25.3:

## 1. Set Up Browserless Tests with Spring Boot
----
Framework: common
Heading: Extend a Base Class Instead
Document Path: v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/setup-spring-boot.md (use get_full_document to get complete context)
----

A test can also extend `SpringBrowserlessTest`, which creates the Vaadin environment with one user and one window before each test method, and closes it afterwards.
The test then calls the window methods on itself:  
`HelloWorldViewTest.java`  

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import com.vaadin.browserless.SpringBrowserlessTest;
import com.vaadin.flow.component.notification.Notification;

@SpringBootTest
class HelloWorldViewTest extends SpringBrowserlessTest {

    @Test
    public void setText_clickButton_notificationIsShown() {
        final HelloWorldView helloView = navigate(HelloWorldView.class);

        test(helloView.name).setValue("Test");
        test(helloView.sayHello).click();

        Notification notification = find(Notification.class).single();
        Assertions.assertEquals("Hello Test", test(notification).getText());
    }

}
```

The base class scans the whole classpath for routes, unless the test class has a `@ViewPackages` annotation.
It applies Spring Security test annotations, such as `@WithMockUser`, to its user; see [Use Spring Security Test Annotations](v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/test-view-access.md).
See [Base Classes](v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/index.md) for when to choose a base class.

================

## 2. Set Up Browserless Tests with Spring Boot
----
Framework: common
Heading: Run the Test
Document Path: v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/setup-spring-boot.md (use get_full_document to get complete context)
----

Run the test from your IDE or with `mvn test`.
The test passes when entering a name and clicking the button shows the expected notification.

================

## 3. Set Up Browserless Tests with Spring Boot
----
Framework: common
Heading: Create a Test > Write the Test
Document Path: v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/setup-spring-boot.md (use get_full_document to get complete context)
----

@Test
    void setText_clickButton_notificationIsShown() {
        window.navigate(HelloWorldView.class); // (4)

window.findTextField().withLabel("Your name").setValue("Test");
        window.findButton().withText("Say hello").click();

Assertions.assertEquals("Hello Test",
                window.findNotification().getText());
    }

}
```

1. Spring injects the shared browserless application context.

2. Creates a user with its own Vaadin session, and opens a window for that user. The window shows the root route.

3. Closes the user and its window after the test. This ends the user's session, and clears the Vaadin state, such as `UI.getCurrent()`, from the test thread, so that the next test starts clean.

4. The test drives the UI through the window: it finds components by their label or text, and types and clicks, as a user does.

Place the test in `src/test/java`, in the same Java package as the view.
See [How a Browserless Test Works](v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/test-user-interactions.md) for what each line of the test method does.  
The tests share one Vaadin service, as the users of a running application do, and each test has a user and a session of its own.
The application context is bound to the thread that creates it, so the tests must run on that thread, as they do with JUnit's default sequential execution.

================

## 4. Debug a Failing Browserless Test
----
Framework: common
Heading: Read the Tree of a Failed Query
Document Path: v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/debug-tests.md (use get_full_document to get complete context)
----

```
└── MockedUI[]
    └── GreetingView[@theme='spacing']
        ├── TextField[label='Your name', value='', manualValidation='true']
        └── Button[caption='Say hello']
            └── Text[text='Say hello']
```

Now you can see:  
* There's no `Notification` in the tree --- the click didn't produce one.

* The `TextField` has `value=''` --- the name field is empty.

* Looking back at the view code, the click handler only opens the notification when the name is nonempty. The test forgot to set the name before clicking.

Set the name before clicking the button, then rerun the test:

```java
window.findTextField().withLabel("Your name").setValue("World");
window.findButton().withText("Say hello").click();
Assertions.assertEquals("Hello World", window.findNotification().getText());
```

See [Snapshot Format](v25.3/flow/testing/browserless/snapshots.md) for the properties represented in the tree.

================

## 5. Test User Interactions
----
Framework: common
Heading: How a Browserless Test Works
Document Path: v25.3/building-apps/testing/browserless/test-user-interactions.md (use get_full_document to get complete context)
----

Each setup guide ends with a test for the same `HelloWorldView`.
The test navigates to the view, enters a name, clicks a button, and checks the notification that appears:  

```java
window.navigate(HelloWorldView.class);

window.findTextField().withLabel("Your name").setValue("Test");
window.findButton().withText("Say hello").click();

Assertions.assertEquals("Hello Test", window.findNotification().getText());
```

The test does everything through `window`, a `BrowserlessUIContext` that represents one browser window of one user.
The following sections explain each step.
They work the same way with every setup; only the code that creates the application context differs.

I added the HelloAgentWorld view and a test for it. All 6 tests pass (5 new, plus the existing `ApplicationTest`). I haven't started the app to check it in a browser.

**View:** `src/main/java/dev/vaadin/agentdemo/hello/HelloAgentWorldView.java`
- It's at `/hello-agent-world` and has a "Name" text field and a "Show" button. The button uses the primary style, and pressing Enter also clicks it.
- Clicking it shows "Hello <name>!" as a success notification in the bottom right for 3 seconds. Spaces before and after the name are removed first.
- **Empty input:** if the field is empty or only spaces, no notification appears. Instead the field turns red with "Please enter a name" and gets focus. The error clears as soon as you type.
- **Navigation:** it's added to the side menu as "Hello Agent World" with a hand icon. The app already builds its side menu from views that declare a menu entry, so I didn't have to change the main layout.

**Test:** `src/test/java/dev/vaadin/agentdemo/hello/HelloAgentWorldViewTest.java` runs without a browser. It checks:
- the notification text, position and success style;
- that the name is trimmed;
- that empty and spaces-only input show no notification and mark the field invalid;
- that the button has the primary style.

The app has no view at `/`, so opening the root URL won't show this view. You need the menu entry or `/hello-agent-world`. If you want it as the start page, I can add `/` as a second address for it.

I haven't committed anything.
